name: scry
description: Session-start checks for codebase architecture, running stack, repository health, concurrent activity, machine pressure, and untrusted Markdown. Requires every dispatch to a model to choose that model rather than inherit a default silently — subagents, workflow agents, and metered agent CLIs invoked through Bash — warns on first contact with a large and actively-worked source file, and guards expensive Elixir force-rebuilds. Tells a spawned subagent when the worktree it was handed is behind origin/main, notes when a session writes Markdown this repo's conventions do not expect, and reports once per session what the session is leaving behind — finished build worktrees still occupying disk, and the scratch Markdown written since the session started. A PreToolUse ADVISORY speaks when a Bash command creates a branch without naming a start point, giving how far HEAD sits behind origin/<default> and how old the last fetch is, since a count measured against a stale remote-tracking ref is itself stale; SCRY_BRANCH_POINT_FETCH_HOURS (default 2) sets when a fetch counts as dated. It never fetches, moves nothing, and denies nothing. A plugin monitor (Claude only) watches when the session's prompt cache goes cold — read from the status-line payload, the only place Claude Code reports it, via a small wrapper the user points statusLine at once — and, at most once per user message, asks the session to write a handoff while the cache is still warm; a UserPromptSubmit hook is what re-arms it, so tool calls, cache hits, and the handoff itself never do. SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF=0 disables it; SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF_LEAD_SECONDS (default 120) sets how long before expiry it speaks. The same status-line wrapper shows the cache at the end of the bar: minutes until it goes cold, and the size of the re-read the next request pays once it has. After /clear, the SessionStart fleet check names the session just left (id, title, resume command) and prints the handoff written for it, if any — the live-window rule otherwise hid exactly that session.

interface.shortDescription: See repository and machine state at session start
interface.longDescription: Adds session-start context about codebase architecture, the stack the system actually runs on, repository hygiene, concurrent Claude and Codex activity, local machine pressure, and why every repository Markdown file is untrusted historical material. Also installs one PreToolUse hook that DENIES a first attempt at an artifact-discarding Elixir rebuild (`mix compile --force`, `rm -rf _build`) and states its cost; running the command again within five minutes passes through untouched. Set SCRY_BUILD_GUARD=0 to disable that hook. A second PreToolUse hook DENIES any dispatch that names no model, because a blank model is not a default -- it silently inherits whatever default is already in place, for the whole run, multiplied across a fan-out. That covers Agent and Workflow dispatch, and metered agent CLIs run through Bash, where an unflagged call falls back to the CLI's own config default; SCRY_METERED_CLIS (default codex) sets which CLIs are covered and SCRY_METERED_CLI_GUARD=0 switches that part off. No model is forbidden; only the absent choice is. On the same surface, a headless `claude -p` run while ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set is refused ONCE with what it will bill -- that run is metered against the API account rather than the subscription -- and the same command repeated within five minutes proceeds; SCRY_API_BILLING_GUARD=0 silences it. A PostToolUse note reports what a premium model draws after it is deliberately chosen, and SCRY_PREMIUM_MODELS sets which models draw it. A further PostToolUse advisory speaks on first contact with a source file that is both large and actively worked, naming what it did not return and what goes wrong silently at that size. Two further ADVISORY hooks inject context and never deny anything. A SubagentStart hook tells a spawned subagent that the worktree it was handed is behind origin/main, by how many commits and days, and how to read the live tip instead -- SessionStart context does not reach a subagent, so an agent otherwise searches a stale tree and reports a feature missing when it merely is not checked out; it fires only when that worktree is on the default branch, it never fetches, and it never moves a ref or a file. A PostToolUse ADVISORY notes, at most once per file, that a Markdown file a session just created is not one this repo's conventions expect and that scratch Markdown may be cleared out at session end; it is silent on README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, GitHub community-health files, anything under .claude/, and on any repo whose product is Markdown content. A Stop hook reports, at most once per session, what the session is leaving behind: how many linked worktrees the repo has, roughly what they occupy and how many hold branches already merged into origin/main (only when something is reclaimable or the pile is large), and the untracked Markdown files in the session's own tree written since it started, named from the same exemption list the creation notice uses. It names the cleanup command and lists the files. SessionEnd would be the obvious event for that and its output reaches no one, which is why it is on Stop; SCRY_WORKTREE_REMINDER_MINUTES (default 45) sets how long a session must run before it speaks, SCRY_WORKTREE_DISK_MB_WARN (default 2048) the size at which an unmerged pile is worth saying out loud, SCRY_SCRATCH_MD_LIST_MAX (default 5) how many Markdown files are named before the rest become a count. It deletes nothing -- no worktree, no file. A PreToolUse ADVISORY speaks when a Bash command creates a branch without naming a start point, giving how far HEAD sits behind origin/<default> and how old the last fetch is, since a count measured against a stale remote-tracking ref is itself stale; SCRY_BRANCH_POINT_FETCH_HOURS (default 2) sets when a fetch counts as dated.
